question: What do elevated triglyceride levels mark?
answer: Elevated triglyceride levels are associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular events. They can be managed or reduced through treatments such as high-dose EPA (icosapent ethyl) and fenofibrate, which have been shown to lower triglyceride levels in patients.

sources.title: The Role of Triglycerides in Atherosclerosis: Recent Pathophysiologic Insights and Therapeutic Implications
sources.evidenceText: REDUCE-IT (Reduction of Cardiovascular Events with Icosapent Ethyl–Intervention Trial): This trial randomized 8,179 patients with elevated triglyceride levels despite statin therapy to high-dose EPA (icosapent ethyl) or placebo.

sources.title: Effects of Fenofibrate Treatment on Cardiovascular Disease Risk in 9,795 Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes and Various Components of the Metabolic Syndrome
sources.evidenceText: In a short-term study, fenofibrate was effective in lowering postprandial triglyceride levels, particularly when metabolic syndrome and elevated triglyceride levels were present.
